title: Mixed conditionals
note: mixed 2nd/3rd (past->present, present->past) + if-alternatives unless / provided that / as long as / in case · 4 strands x 12 · 48 items · built to live 2026-08-06 (cloud run 5)

cards.title: One condition, two different times
cards.body: The second conditional is unreal **now**; the third is unreal **in the past**. A **mixed** conditional takes one half from each, because the cause and the result belong to different times.
cards.body_cz: Druhý kondicionál je nereálný **teď**, třetí **v minulosti**. **Smíšený** kondicionál bere z každého jednu polovinu, protože příčina a výsledek patří do jiného času.

table.caption: The two mixed patterns
rows: if + past perfect, would + base form
If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.
if + past simple, would have + past participle
If I were faster, I would have finished it yesterday.

cards.title: Past cause, present result
cards.body: Something did not happen, and you are living with the consequence today. The if-clause is **past perfect**; the result is **would + base form**.
cards.body_cz: Něco se nestalo a vy dnes žijete s následkem. Věta s if je v **předminulém čase**, výsledek je **would + základní tvar**.
points: If we had bought that house, we would live in the city centre now.
If I had gone to bed earlier, I would not be tired now.
The result clause has no have — that is what makes it present.

cards.title: Present cause, past result
cards.body: Something is permanently true about you, and it explains a past event. The if-clause is **past simple** (or **were**); the result is **would have + past participle**.
cards.body_cz: Něco o vás platí trvale a vysvětluje to minulou událost. Věta s if je v **minulém prostém** (nebo **were**), výsledek je **would have + příčestí minulé**.
points: If she spoke English, she would have got that job last year.
If I did not live so far away, I would have come to your party.
After if, were is used for every person: if he were, if I were.

cards.title: The time word decides
cards.body: Read the result clause before you choose. Words like **now**, **today** and **by now** mean **would + base form**; **yesterday**, **last year** and **on time** mean **would have + past participle**.
cards.body_cz: Než si vyberete, přečtěte si výslednou větu. Slova jako **now**, **today** a **by now** znamenají **would + základní tvar**; **yesterday**, **last year** a **on time** znamenají **would have + příčestí minulé**.

table.caption: Same condition, two results
rows: … I would not be in this trouble now.
… I would not have made that mistake.

cards.title: unless · provided that · as long as · in case
cards.title_cz: unless · provided that · as long as · in case
cards.body: These four replace **if** and each changes the meaning. **unless** means *if not*, so the verb after it stays positive. **in case** is a precaution taken **before** anything happens — it is not a condition at all.
cards.body_cz: Tyto čtyři nahrazují **if** a každé mění význam. **unless** znamená *pokud ne*, takže sloveso za ním zůstává kladné. **in case** je opatření **předem**, není to vůbec podmínka.

table.caption: What each one means
rows: We will be late unless we leave now.
You can borrow my car provided that you drive carefully.
You can stay as long as you help with the cooking.
Take an umbrella in case it rains.

points: Never put not after unless: not "unless he does not come".
in case it rains = take it now · if it rains = take it only when it starts.
